dek.text: Dell Med's AI Learning Lab gives half of its 80 clinicians Claude and the other half UpToDate with its AI switched off, then watches how each group reasons.

introduction.text: [The IC² Institute and Dell Medical School announced the AI Learning Lab on {{date:c1}}](c1). [The announcement said it would launch later that month with {{number:c2}} Dell Med clinicians](c2). [They are a mix of faculty, residents and students, and they meet patients in simulated encounters](c3).

[Half of the clinicians have Claude to help diagnose the patient](c4). [The other half rely on UpToDate, a web based medical encyclopedia, with its AI capability disabled](c5). The study is built around that one difference.

sections.heading: A live patient, played by an actor

paragraphs.text: [The patients are paid actors presenting a medical issue](c6). [Each clinician meets the patient, asks questions, synthesizes information and arrives at a diagnosis](c7). [The lab uses a live encounter rather than a written case on a page](c12). [Researcher Tu-Quyen Dao says a large part of solving a real case is interacting with the patient to gather information](c13).

[Researchers will observe and compare the clinical reasoning of both groups and analyze AI use across experience levels](c8). [They plan to use measurements and rubrics, observation and an analysis of post encounter interviews](c16).

Researcher Sookja Kang names the questions. [How quickly do participants click on their AI tool](c9)? [Do they passively accept AI output or actively interrogate it](c10)? [How much reasoning work gets handed off to the AI tool as the diagnosis evolves](c11)? [The project page lists a taxonomy of the ways clinicians engage with large language models among its aims](c19), [along with naming new clinician skills that grow out of reasoning alongside AI](c20).

sections.heading: Why a medical school is asking now

paragraphs.text: [The release cites a {{number:c15}} American Medical Association survey in which {{number:c15:1}}% of doctors use AI in practice, against {{number:c15:2}}% reported in {{number:c15:3}}](c15). That figure is the release's citation and not a finding of the lab. [Dell Med's Vice Dean of Education James Korndorffer says AI is going to be used and should be](c14).

[The release says results could help Dell Med and other schools decide how and when AI enters the curriculum](c17). Neither the announcement nor the project page reports any result or gives a date for one, so the record can't yet say how either group reasoned.
